# Dry run, reads only. 26,239 rows walked: 24,924 relocatable, 1,315 with no vector at all.

# THE BACKFILL CANNOT REPAIR THESE. A relocation moves a row's own vector from the legacy slot
# into the named space; a row with no vector has nothing to move. They need a RE-EMBED.
#
# ── BUT THE COUNT IS MISLEADING AND THE SPLIT IS THE POINT ──────────────────────────────────
#
# 1,299 of the 1,315 are RDF BLANK NODES (N<hex>), whose only text is their own hex id. I first
# read that as "the vectorless rows are blank nodes" — WRONG, and a sample said so: of 200
# blank nodes sampled, 193 DO carry a vector. Blank nodes are not the vectorless population;
# they are simply most of the index.
#
#     OntologyClass    26,239 rows
#       blank nodes    25,255   (96.2% of the routing index)   1,299 without a vector
#       real URIs         984                                     16 without a vector
#
# So the actionable re-embed work is SIXTEEN CLASSES, listed first below. The 1,299 blank nodes
# are a different question — whether anonymous RDF nodes belong in a retrieval index at all —
# and that is an INGEST FILTER decision for doc-tools, not a re-embed.
#
# IT DOES NOT BLOCK THE BACKFILL. Measured after: scoring "what hazards are unattended" against
# all 12,512 vectorised SUSTAINMENT rows puts safety#Hazard at RANK 1 (cos 0.659), with ZERO
# blank nodes above it and zero in the top 10. Their hex labels embed far from natural language.
